gallery.filename: Stone block with Paikuli inscription.JPG
gallery.title: File:Stone block with Paikuli inscription.JPG
gallery.description: This stone block from the Paikuli tower was inscribed with middle Persian language. The block is on display in the Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq. One of the two inscribed blocks on display in the Sulaymaniyah Museum. The middle Persian language was used on this stone block. (Block No. PK 22; on tower No. D3 ; 56.51 x 48 x 26 cm; SM2696; acquisition year 1997)

gallery.title: File:Earrings from Shulgi.JPG
gallery.description: The cuneiform inscriptions on this pair of earrings state that these earrings were a gift from king Shulgi. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq. A Pair of Golden Earrings from the Time of Shulgi, the second King of Ur III Dynasty (2093-2046 BC)

gallery.filename: Tablet V of the Epic of Gilgamesh.jpg
gallery.title: File:Tablet V of the Epic of Gilgamesh.jpg
gallery.source: Tablet V of the Epic of Gilgamesh
gallery.description: This is a newly discovered partially broken tablet V of the Epic of Gilgamesh. The tablet dates back to the old Babylonian period, 2003-1595 BCE; Neo-Babylonian period according to the edition in F. Al-Rawi et A. R. George, « Back to the Cedar Forest: The beginning and end of Tablet V of the Standard Babylonian Epic of Gilgameš », Journal of Cuneiform Studies, vol. 66,‎ 2014, pp. 69-90. From Mesopotamia, Iraq. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq.

gallery.description: This pottery head of a stand was inscribed with a cuneiform inscription mentioning the name of the Entemena (Enmetena), ruler of Lagash, and dates back to the Early Dynastic Period, C. 2400 BCE. From Southern Mesopotamia, modern-day Iraq. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq.

gallery.filename: "The lady at the window," one of the famous Nimrud ivories' plaques. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq..JPG
gallery.title: File:"The lady at the window," one of the famous Nimrud ivories' plaques. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq..JPG
gallery.source: "The lady at the window," one of the famous Nimrud ivories' plaques. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq.
gallery.description: “Woman at the window” or “the lady of the window” is one of the most famous scenes in Phoenician ivory carving. The plaque shows a woman who looks out of a window, thought to be a sacred prostitute linked to the goddess Astarte or Ishtar. However, the exact significance of the scene is still unknown. Neo-Assyrian period, 9th-7th centuries BCE. From Nimrud, Mesopotamia, Iraq. The Sulaimaniyah Museum, Iraq.

gallery.title: File:6. Detail. Jewish tombstone of Siporah daughter of Dan, from Gopala, Sulaymaniyah, Iraq, c. 1356-1357 CE. Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraqi Kurdistan.jpg
gallery.description: Detail. This irregularly-shaped rock is an inscribed (in Hebrew) tombstone of a deceased Jewish woman. Her name was "Siporah daughter of Dan" who will rest in peace and be blessed in the Paradise of Eden. Commissioned by her son. The date on the tombstone is the Seleucian year 1669 (and that would be roughly 1356/1357 CE). From Gopala village, Bazian (Baziyan), Sulaymaniyah Governorate, Iraq. Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraqi Kurdistan.
categories: Jewish tombstone of Siporah daughter of Dan
